title: F-Droid 2.0
summary:
F-Droid 2.0 marks the official F-Droid app's largest update in a decade, featuring a complete redesign and rewrite in Kotlin Compose for a modern interface and improved user experience. It aims to make discovering, installing, and managing free and open-source Android apps easier.

The main interface is streamlined into "Discover," "Search," and "My Apps." Discoverability is significantly enhanced with a redesigned Discover page highlighting recent, updated, and most downloaded apps. Categories have been greatly expanded and refined, including higher-level "meta" categories and granular types like 17 specific game genres. Search capabilities are improved, now indexing app descriptions, categories, and translations, with better CJK language support and recent search memory. Powerful, guided filtering allows users to combine multiple criteria for precise app discovery.

Installation is smoother, leveraging new Android APIs for a unified, pre-authorized experience akin to built-in app stores. Automatic background update checks are now standard, replacing the pull-to-refresh gesture for updates (manual options remain). Privacy features include simplified Tor integration (recommending Tor VPN) and "panic" functions. The app hiding feature has been adjusted to only change the icon and name, clarifying its limitations compared to the previous calculator disguise. The Ripple-triggered app removal/wiping feature has been removed due to high maintenance and low usage, with feedback sought on its importance. F-Droid 2.0 no longer supports Android 6 or the F-Droid Privileged Extension, relying on Android's session installer for background updates.

Under the hood, the modern codebase (Kotlin, Jetpack Compose) lowers the barrier for new contributors. This ambitious project involved extensive community effort, user research, design, testing, and a security audit, supported by organizations like NLnet and Open Technology Fund. F-Droid 2.0 is a milestone, not an end, with ongoing work planned for performance, accessibility, and a redesigned "Nearby" app-sharing feature. Users are encouraged to provide feedback, contribute to testing and development, and donate to support the project's sustainability.
chinese_title: F-Droid 2.0
chinese_summary:
F-Droid 2.0 标志着 F-Droid 官方应用十年来最大规模的一次更新，它使用 Kotlin Compose 进行了彻底的重新设计和重写，带来了现代化的界面和改进的用户体验。此版本旨在让发现、安装和管理免费开源 Android 应用变得更简单。

主界面精简为“发现”、“搜索”和“我的应用”。通过重新设计的“发现”页面，突出显示最新、已更新和下载最多的应用，显著增强了应用发现能力。分类已大大扩展和完善，包括更高层的“元”类别和更细化的类型，例如17种特定的游戏流派。搜索功能得到改进，现在能索引应用描述、类别和翻译，更好地支持中日韩语言并具有近期搜索记忆功能。强大的引导式过滤允许用户组合多个条件，以精确发现应用。

安装过程更流畅，利用新的 Android API 提供类似于内置应用商店的统一、预授权体验。自动后台更新检查现在成为标准功能，取代了下拉刷新以检查更新的手势（手动选项仍然保留）。隐私功能包括简化的 Tor 集成（推荐 Tor VPN）和“恐慌”功能。应用隐藏功能已调整为仅更改图标和名称，澄清了其与之前计算器伪装相比的局限性。由于维护成本高且使用率低，“Ripple”触发的应用删除/擦除功能已被移除，并就其重要性征求反馈。F-Droid 2.0 不再支持 Android 6 或 F-Droid 特权扩展，转而依赖 Android 的会话安装器进行后台更新。

在底层，现代代码库（Kotlin, Jetpack Compose）降低了新贡献者的门槛。这个雄心勃勃的项目涉及广泛的社区努力、用户研究、设计、测试和安全审计，得到了 NLnet 和开放技术基金等组织的支持。F-Droid 2.0 是一个里程碑，而不是终点，计划继续进行性能、辅助功能以及重新设计的“附近分享”应用共享功能的工作。鼓励用户提供反馈，为测试和开发做出贡献，并捐款以支持项目的可持续性。

title: Dutch governments builds alternative for Microsoft based on NixOS
summary:
The DAWO (Digitally Autonomous Workplace) community is a collaborative Dutch initiative uniting government, industry, and society to build a digitally autonomous workplace for the national government. Its primary aim is to reduce reliance on single vendors, thereby strengthening the digital sovereignty of the Netherlands.

DAWO's five core goals include: bolstering digital autonomy, enhancing collaboration and knowledge sharing, ensuring security and data protection, fostering innovation, and making government IT systems more verifiable and inspectable.

The project's methodology centers on developing an open workplace composed of replaceable and inspectable building blocks, rather than a monolithic product. These modular components cover key areas such as open and verifiable AI, the DAWO-NixOS operating system for reproducible environments, autonomous cloud infrastructure, and open solutions for communication and collaboration.

The community emphasizes transparency and active participation, providing public access to events, news, a blog, and a forum through its member portal. DAWO encourages engagement via conversations, code contributions, documentation, pilots, and events, embodying its philosophy of building "Not for the community. With the community." This collaborative model seeks to establish a resilient and open government IT ecosystem.
chinese_title: 荷兰政府基于NixOS构建微软替代方案
chinese_summary:
DAWO（数字化自治工作场所）社区是一个荷兰的合作倡议，它联合政府、行业和社会，旨在为荷兰国家政府构建一个数字化自治工作场所。其主要目标是减少对单一供应商的依赖，从而加强荷兰的数字主权。

DAWO的五大核心目标包括：增强数字自治能力、促进协作和知识共享、确保安全和数据保护、培养创新，以及提高政府IT系统的可验证性和可检查性。

该项目的方法论侧重于开发一个由可替换和可检查的构建模块组成的开放工作场所，而非一个单一的整体产品。这些模块化组件涵盖了关键领域，例如开放且可验证的AI、用于可复现环境的DAWO-NixOS操作系统、自治云基础设施，以及用于通信和协作的开放解决方案。

社区强调透明度和积极参与，通过其成员门户提供对活动、新闻、博客和论坛的公开访问。DAWO鼓励通过对话、代码贡献、文档、试点项目和活动进行参与，体现其“不是为社区，而是与社区一同建设”的理念。这种协作模式旨在建立一个有弹性且开放的政府IT生态系统。

title: Meta takes down a critical video about meta AI Glasses after filming at Meta
summary:
The Reddit post, titled "Meta takes down a critical video about meta AI Glasses after filming at Meta," was published 10 years ago. The original poster explicitly stated that they could not find the actual video content being referenced, only discussions about its alleged removal.

The comments section of the post largely critiques the historical accuracy of the title itself. Users point out that the company was known as Facebook, not "Meta," a decade ago, and "AI Glasses" as they are understood today did not exist at that time. Many comments therefore suggest that the title is anachronistic or misinformed, casting doubt on the premise of the post. In essence, the Reddit thread functions more as a discussion questioning the details of a claimed incident rather than a report on an event with confirmed facts.

title: Why is the liver so weirdly regenerative?
summary:
The article "Why is the liver so weirdly regenerative?" explores the unique regenerative capabilities of the liver, contrasting it with other organs and questioning the evolutionary reasons behind this extraordinary trait.

The author notes that while many organs can heal or repair, the liver is one of the few that can regrow significant portions of itself. This ability isn't about stem cells in the typical sense; rather, existing liver cells (hepatocytes) can dedifferentiate, proliferate, and then redifferentiate to restore lost tissue. This process is remarkably robust, allowing the liver to fully regenerate even after losing up to 70% of its mass.

The article delves into potential evolutionary explanations. While common injuries like cuts or broken bones might select for healing mechanisms, it's less clear why such extensive regeneration would be necessary for an internal organ like the liver. It suggests that perhaps the liver's role in detoxification exposes it to unique, severe damage, making regeneration a critical survival mechanism. Toxins, whether ingested or produced metabolically, can cause widespread liver cell death, necessitating a rapid and comprehensive repair system.

The author speculates that other organs might not have evolved similar regenerative capacity because their typical modes of failure (e.g., heart disease, brain injury) don't align with this type of "patch-and-grow-back" solution, or perhaps the energetic cost of such regeneration outweighs the benefits for those organs. The liver's constant exposure to harmful substances, therefore, might be the key driver behind its "weirdly regenerative" nature.
chinese_title: 为什么肝脏的再生能力如此奇特？
chinese_summary:
文章《为什么肝脏的再生能力如此奇特？》探讨了肝脏独特的再生能力，将其与其他器官进行对比，并探究了这一非凡特性的进化原因。

作者指出，尽管许多器官可以愈合或修复，但肝脏是少数能够再生出大部分自身组织的器官之一。这种能力并非通常意义上的干细胞作用；相反，现有的肝细胞（hepatocytes）可以去分化、增殖，然后重新分化以恢复丢失的组织。这一过程极其强大，即使在失去高达70%的质量后，肝脏也能完全再生。

文章深入探讨了潜在的进化解释。尽管割伤或骨折等常见损伤可能会促使愈合机制的选择，但对于肝脏这样的内脏器官来说，为何需要如此广泛的再生能力则不那么清楚。文章推测，或许肝脏在解毒中的作用使其面临独特而严重的损伤，从而使再生能力成为一种关键的生存机制。毒素，无论是摄入的还是代谢产生的，都可能导致肝细胞广泛死亡，这就要求一个快速而全面的修复系统。

作者推测，其他器官可能没有进化出类似的再生能力，因为它们典型的衰竭模式（例如心脏病、脑损伤）与这种“修补和再生”的解决方案不符，或者，这种再生的能量成本对于这些器官来说可能大于其益处。因此，肝脏持续暴露于有害物质，可能是其“奇特再生”特性的关键驱动因素。

title: Two-tier encryption in the UK
summary:
The article describes a "two-tier" encryption system for Apple users in the UK, stemming from a conflict between Apple's Advanced Data Protection (ADP) and the UK government. Apple has a long history of resisting government demands for backdoors, notably during the 2015 San Bernardino case, where it refused to weaken its encryption.

In 2025, the UK government reportedly issued a secret Technical Capability Notice (TCN) under its Investigatory Powers Act 2016, demanding Apple create a way to access iCloud data protected by ADP. ADP provides end-to-end encryption for sensitive data categories (like Photos and Backups), meaning Apple *does not* possess the decryption keys. Unlike standard iCloud encryption, which Apple can decrypt, ADP-protected data is inaccessible to the company.

Apple's response, without confirming the TCN, was to cease offering ADP to *new* UK users from February 2025. Apple maintained its stance against creating backdoors. Crucially, due to ADP's design, Apple could not unilaterally disable it for *existing* UK users who had already enabled the feature.

This created the "two-tier" system: existing users (like "Alice") who enabled ADP before the cutoff retain stronger end-to-end encryption, while new users or those who missed the opt-in window (like "Bill") cannot enable it.

The author criticizes the secrecy of TCNs and the government's demand for a "technical capability" that would fundamentally alter encryption architecture, effectively requiring a backdoor. Apple's decision to withdraw ADP for new UK users is presented as a difficult but necessary move to avoid compromising security for all users globally, highlighting the ongoing tension between national security demands and individual privacy in a free society.
chinese_title: Two-tier encryption in the UK
chinese_summary:
文章描述了针对英国苹果用户的“两级”加密系统，源于苹果高级数据保护（ADP）与英国政府之间的冲突。苹果长期以来一直抵制政府对后门的需求，尤其是在2015年圣贝纳迪诺案中，苹果拒绝削弱其加密技术。

据报道，2025年，英国政府根据其《2016年调查权力法》发布了一份秘密的“技术能力通知”（TCN），要求苹果创建一种方法来访问受ADP保护的iCloud数据。ADP为敏感数据类别（如照片和备份）提供端到端加密，这意味着苹果*不*拥有解密密钥。与苹果可以解密的标准iCloud加密不同，受ADP保护的数据对该公司来说是不可访问的。

苹果的回应是，在不确认TCN的情况下，从2025年2月起停止向*新的*英国用户提供ADP。苹果坚持其反对创建后门的立场。至关重要的是，由于ADP的设计，苹果无法单方面禁用已经启用该功能的*现有*英国用户的ADP。

这就创建了“两级”系统：在截止日期前启用ADP的现有用户（如“爱丽丝”）保留了更强的端到端加密，而新用户或错过了选择启用窗口的用户（如“比尔”）则无法启用ADP。

作者批评TCN的保密性，以及政府要求一种将从根本上改变加密架构的“技术能力”，这实际上是要求一个后门。苹果决定撤回面向英国新用户的ADP，被认为是避免损害全球所有用户安全的艰难但必要之举，凸显了自由社会中国家安全需求与个人隐私之间持续存在的紧张关系。
